description: Agent Capacity: submit the throttling rules for work that arrives at capacity, with the requests: the rules with each priority class, its rank (1 served first) and what it does at capacity (admit, defer or refuse), how soon a deferred or refused requester is told in hours, and the rules as written, read for wording such as case by case, best effort or at our discretion; and each request with its id, its class, when it arrived, whether it arrived at capacity, its outcome (admitted, deferred or refused), when work on it started and when the requester was told. The signed report gives the classes in rank order with the discretionary wording found, every request with its rank, its class rule and whether it followed the rule at capacity, every pair where a lower class was admitted at capacity while a higher class that arrived no later waited or was turned away, and every deferred or refused request with when the requester was told, and counts them, and names throttling that is absent: no written priority class, a priority inversion at capacity and a deferred or refused requester never told; then discretionary wording, a request handled against its class rule, notice after the window, a request in an unlisted class and two classes on one rank, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No requests, no record of which arrived at capacity, no notice window or no rules text leaves the throttling unverified. This reads admission at capacity against written priority classes: the order queue items are ranked in against severity and impact is wever_triage-priority-check, how each queue item ends with its deferral reason and return date is wever_triage-disposition-check and where work goes at a spending limit is wever_breach-path-check. Verdict capacity_throttle_absent, capacity_throttle_partial, capacity_throttle_unverified or capacity_throttle_ordered. POST /api/capacity-throttle-check. Reads the load and capacity records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Capacity reads an agent’s own load and capacity records and checks the load against the capacity that exists: work in hand against the stated limit, a queue against its target wait, concurrent runs against the cap, an allowance’s burn against its period, a backlog across a window, spare capacity against the reserve, the scaling plan against the burn, and admission at capacity against written priority rules. Beside it, the Agent Limits checks such as wever_limit-substrate-check read whether a limit sits in code or in prose and how it is scoped, changed and seen, while a capacity check reads the load itself against the capacity; wever_commitment-deadline-check reads promised hours against due dates, while the workload check reads the work in hand against the stated limit over time; and the Agent Triage checks such as wever_triage-priority-check read how queue items are ranked, reviewed and closed, while the queue, backlog and throttle checks read waits, size and admission against capacity. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-capacity-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-capacity/.
